action: As Bell advises, be wary of unsolicited requests for personal information and of links or attachments in suspicious emails or texts, and check accounts regularly.
date_note: VOCM (published 23 November) says the data was accessed in the attack on November 17th; Bell's own notice was not read.
exec: Bell says an "agentic threat actor" accessed internal systems with customer personal information; the RCMP's cyber crime unit has been contacted.
plain: Bell says an intruder it calls an "agentic threat actor" got into some internal systems that held customers' personal information. It says bank and credit card numbers were not affected.

sources.name: VOCM: RCMP Investigating Bell Cybersecurity Incident
PortageOnline.com: Bell cybersecurity breach disclosed after email outage

summary: VOCM reports that Bell says an "agentic threat actor" accessed some of its internal systems in an attack on 17 November. PortageOnline says Bell states names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, account numbers, product details and recent payment dates and amounts could have been exposed. Bell says credit card and bank account information were not affected. Bell says it has engaged the RCMP's cybercrime unit.
title: Bell says an "agentic threat actor" accessed internal systems with customer information; RCMP cyber crime unit contacted

validation.note: VOCM and PortageOnline (two publishers) each relay Bell's statement that an unauthorized party accessed an internal system on 17 November and that card and bank data were not affected; Bell's own notice (bell.ca/cybernotice) was not read.

review.note: stronger than the source: removed unsupported 'Bell is notifying customers'; could have been exposed per Bell; action matches Bell advice on VOCM
